Maps/Visual : This game has some of the most INCREDIBLE map design/scenery I've ever seen. It's really breathtaking. I find myself constantly looking around amazed with how dang cool this game looks. The verticality on both maps is insane. You can take advantage of it frequently to dispatch squads as a solo, and outplay people. It opens of a lot of scenarios where you actually have to make difficult decisions in how you traverse the map. Even with strong map knowledge I always find new routes and and ways to approach the places I want to go.

Gunplay/Equipment : The gunplay is solid. I'd say it's a mix of Apex and COD, biased towards the Apex side of things. The armor and weapons are in a decent state, but they are constantly being tuned in the right direction (IMO). You have weapons that are better for PvE or PvP, which can make for some interesting loadouts as a solo player. The weapons get better as you progress but it isn't super unfairly weighted towards mid/high tier weapons, although there is definitely an advantage to running a good kit. The attachment system could use a little work in the UI area but overall it's going in a good direction. The common armor is cheap and readily available, so you don't have to worry about going in without any. The good armor isn't hard to craft at all, but it isn't just handed to you. Overall, the gear system is in a decent place for them to flesh out...There is a lot of room for them to balance things without ruining the game.

Quests/Progression : Man...There is always something to do in the game. Always. The quests are just open enough to not pidgeonhole you into annoying situations (Like tarkov, kill 9 scavs at night doing a backflip naked). They lead you around both maps in a very good way. Some quests lead you to specific areas to kill stuff, others just ask you to kill stuff anywhere. Some quests ask for items that can be found all over, others that can be found in a specific place etc etc. It isn't always straightforward. There are 0 junk items in this game. Everything will have use in one way or another. You have a lot of freedom to do what you want in this game without hurting your progression. In terms of item loss on death etc, it is punishing when you die but the insurance system is very forgiving. Dying is just a minor set back in this game. 

Cheaters : I've put 100+ hours into this game and only seen one hacker. Most people are calling hacks on legitimate players because they are bad at the game. Full stop.

Squad v Solo : It's totally possible to kill squads as a solo, but you can't just oongaboonga into bad fights. A lot of the complaints like "omg this game is literally unplayable if you aren't in a squad" "unplayable as a solo" are players who take awful fights. This game isn't about always taking fights, it's about using your brain to either take advantage of people's mistakes or dodging fights you can't win. Don't listen to the whining. Play smarter. You aren't a super hero, you can't win every fight in this game.

Overall : Give it a chance. Looter shooters aren't for everyone. This game is free, give it a try and see if you like it. It's a solid 7/10 in my book. The visuals never cease to amaze me and the PvP is adrenaline fueled insanity.

Pro's:

-GREAT ART STYLE.  I like the cel-shaded, cartoon, Borderlands-meets-Outer Space vibe.
-FUN THEME.  Kind of a sci-fi Fallout; creeping through ruins, shooting critters, scavenging loot.
-COOL STORY.  I like the competing corporations thing, and the idea of being a nomadic scavenger that's bringing lost tech and vital supplies back to a space station housing the last of humanity.  Lots there to play with here.

Con's:

-ARTIFICIAL BOTTLENECKS.  Stuff like quests saying "Kill X number of Y critter at Z location."  Game does not tell you that the Y critter respawn rate at Z location is abysmal, resulting in players stacking on an empty objective and then camping/ganking each other while they wait for critter respawn.  This happens a lot.  Like, too much.  Pretty much every other quest for 12 hours did this, to the point where I began to question if this was a deliberate game design choice to force PvP.  Not opposed to PvP, but if this was an intentional decision to force PvP it's a cheap, contrived, and ultimately detrimental way of doing it.
-PAY TO WIN.  Frankly, this is my own fault.  I knew this would be a PTW game as soon as I looked at it in the store, but bit off like an idiot anyway because I liked the pretty colors.  The generation rate on in-game currency is better than some, but you'll never keep up to the schmuck with a loose wallet.  Don't bother trying, you'll just get frustrated.
-HOLLOW.  That thing I said about it having a cool story and setting is true, but it's all on the surface.  No substantial or meaningful NPC interactions, no little journals or lore nuggets to chew on scattered about.  The best you'll get is maybe a spray painted message on a wall that hints at the existence of deeper lore, until you see it again 5 minutes later and realize it means nothing.  

Final thoughts:

This game is the equivalent of being a 5 year old on Easter who sees the most amazing egg, runs up, grabs it, and then finds out that Nana just painted a hard-boiled egg.  It's exactly what it looks like on the surface, but you're still disappointed when you crack it open.

"The Cycle: Frontier" is a unique multiplayer shooter game that offers an interesting blend of PvP and PvE gameplay. Set in the distant future on a dangerous alien planet called Fortuna III, players take on the role of prospectors who are seeking to extract valuable resources while battling against other players and alien creatures.

One of the standout features of The Cycle is the way it seamlessly integrates PvP and PvE elements. As players compete to complete contracts and objectives, they must also defend themselves against hostile alien creatures and other prospectors who are trying to steal their resources. This creates a dynamic and ever-changing gameplay experience that keeps players engaged and on their toes. You may hear shooting in the distance: is that two teams fighting or just one team fighting an alien?

The game also offers a wide range of weapons and abilities that players can unlock and upgrade as they progress. From rifles and shotguns to grenades and end game special perks that can be applied to your gear when you progress through the questline, there are plenty of ways to customize your character and playstyle. Additionally, the game's crafting system allows players to create unique gear and weapons that can give them an edge in combat.

The graphics and sound design in The Cycle are also top-notch. The alien landscape of Fortuna III is richly detailed and filled with stunning vistas, while the sound effects and music help to create an immersive and intense atmosphere.

One potential downside of the game is that it can be a bit repetitive at times, as players are often doing similar tasks and objectives. However, the constantly changing nature of the game and the competitive aspect of the PvP combat help to keep things fresh and exciting.

Overall, The Cycle: Frontier is a well-crafted and engaging multiplayer extraction shooter that offers a unique blend of gameplay mechanics. With its combination of PvE and PvP elements, customizable weapons and abilities, thrill of venturing into the unknown with stunning graphics and sound design, it's a game that's definitely worth checking out given that it is a free title within the extraction shooter genre that is new and upcoming.

Unfortunately at this point I cannot recommend this game to anyone. There are multiple things missing from this game on 2 main areas, Progression and a reliable anti-cheat. I also want to say that im writing this review because I want to see the cycle: frontier survive, although if changes are not made soon I dont believe it will last very long.

The Progression aspect has to do with logarithmic armor, weapon balancing and economy. 

With the armor changes that came out after beta 2 armor barely means anything anymore. The only noticeable change between armors comes between white and blue armor. There is virtually no point in running any armor besides White for low gear runs and Blue for geared runs. Purple and exotic armor do not feel worth it currently with the penetration values on guns and how they interact with the armor in game. So essentially the only reason you would run purple or exotic armor is if you grab some in raid and put insurance on it for a return in profit. 

The weapon balancing is a joke at this point, they have made decent strides in trying to widen the gap between low-tier weapons and high-tier weapons but it still feels as if many changes need to be made to make higher tier guns worth the cost. The manticore is still too good in my opinion, If they swapped the recoil that the advocate has with the manticore both of those guns would feel more in the tiers they are supposed to be in for example. At the moment the higher tier guns are either too expensive for the average player to obtain or require certain mods to make it gain an edge over the lower tier weapons. For example lets take a look at the DMR's in the Cycle. The Basilisk DMR from Osiris has a faction level 18 unlock requirement and costs 275,000 k marks to purchase. It has 34 base damage and 28 base pen with a 1.6 crit multiplier. The KBR on the other hand from Korolev costs 99,000 k marks to purchase and has a level 14 faction level unlock requirement. This gun has 35 base damage (1 more than the Basilisk), 26 pen (2 less than the basilisk) and a crit multiplier of 1.5 (0.1 less than the basilisk). With the armor in the game at its current state, 2 more pen and 0.1 more crit will not net you any super noticeable changes between the two higher end guns. TL;DR is the Basilisk and the KBR essentially do the same thing but with a staggering 176,000 k marks difference in price. Now if we compare both of these weapons to the cheaper option in the DMR class, The Lacerator from ICA, which costs 41,000 k marks and has a unlock requirement of faction level 9 the results are: 27 base damage (7 less than the basilisk and 8 less than the KBR) 23 pen (5 less than the Basilisk and 3 less than the KBR) and a 1.5 crit multiplier (0.1 less than the basilisk and the same as the KBR). With these stats displayed and all of these guns pitted against the best armor in the game with no converters. We can see that It will take 3 bodyshots from the basilisk to kill against exotic armor, 4 bodyshots to kill with the KBR and 5 for the lacerator. Remember this is against the best and hardest to obtain armor in the game, and also the only armor that you will see any noticable difference against. If you look at all of these guns against blue armor, which is basically the PVP standard, the KBR and the Basilisk will both take 3 body shots to kill and the lacerator will take 4. This is not enough gap between the weapons to make any noticeable difference when fighting, especially since buying the lacerator will save you 234,000 k marks and will give you about the same success as the other two options.

With these two points made here comes the economy. After you are not making a (somewhat) steady income from questing the amount of K marks you can make in this game is pretty low. Barring end game content, which is basically gatekept by cheaters anyway (but this is for later), it is hard to make any sort of reasonable and fast increase in your k marks besides getting mob heads to drop on a RNG drop chance. Since this game gets compared to Escape from Tarkov a lot, even though i dont think a direct comparison is necessarily fair, i will make the comparison. In EFT there are certain items you can extract with that have a decent value and can end up making 1-2 mil a raid with selling on the flea or even traders depending on the items. This kind of "come up" is not possible outside of either the aforementioned end game content or the random drop chance heads from AI mobs. This ties directly into why end game guns and armor do not feel worth it to run. They cost too much purchase or craft. At least you get an insurance return on these if you do die with them. which can mitigate the cost a bit if you decide to run any of the weapons for fun.

Now comes the second aspect for why i cannot recommend this game. The Cheaters. You can forget about running the second map ( Crescent Falls) consistently without running into cheaters. They are generally in 1 out of every 5 games i load into, and I wish that was an exaggeration. If anything i was being generous with those odds. Now this may be due to my average loot value brought out of raid, If im correct this is their main MMR seperator between players. Correct me if im wrong. Even on the first map (Bright Sands) its about a 1 in 10 (again being generous) chance to have a cheater in your game. On top of that, these cheaters usually will camp or do the endgame content to gate you out of it. We have called in i believe a total of 5 drills and 2 of them have ended in being killed by blatant cheaters. Hard to recount how many oil pumps we have ran but i can recall at least twice being killed by blatant cheaters. The dungeon/raid on Crescent falls we have ran 4 times and have been killed by cheaters twice camping the exit to the raid. With the current status of cheaters in the game it is very hard to run end game content without the constant stress that you will lose everything without even a fair fight. Which can be a huge quit moment for most players.

So unfortunately, currently this game is not worth getting into. I will change my review in the future if more of these issues get sorted and will continue to play the cycle. I also would like to say this game has the potential to be huge, it is one of the most fun games ive played since the release of the EFT alpha. I hope that the devs can sort this stuff out and give us an amazing player experience but only time will tell.

I want to like this game. I love, absolutely love, the environment design. Unfortunately, the gameplay is in conflict with itself. You go down to the wonderfully detailed planets, kill some aliens and maybe some people, then return. There's a couple of really serious problems with this. The first is that the PVE and PVP elements are in conflict with each other. If you're trying to do a PVE quest, your best option is to completely avoid all players. This is safe and, given there are only a few alien types, very boring. The second is that there is no good reason to every bring your expensive stuff with you. It simply increases the risk to you (potentially exponentially) without granting you any equivalent benefit. The best possible strategy is to go down with cheap gear, kill some aliens, maybe mine some rocks, maybe kill a player if they're unlucky, and then sell everything you don't need for a quest. Repeat indefinitely. There's no real sense of progression because the higher the level of your gear, the less likely it is you will ever want to bring it with you. And your home base, despite being (like every other environment in the game) beautifully detailed, is ultimately lifeless.

The game is meh at best.  It is tarkov with a shittier community, shitty run around lost and fetch quests, no sustainability, and horrible gunplay.

Anyone close enough to you, who can voip to you, will claim friendly.  Did a test today, out of 20 voip interactions, 20 claimed friendly.  Out of the 20 who claimed friendly, 19 shot me as soon as my back was turned.  Out of my 40 matches today,  10 deaths were from a 3 man team, sitting inside a room, and as soon as the door opens, they drop you.  No way to know they are there, no way to defend against it.  Just click the open button, door slides open, blam blam blam, back to lobby.   5 deaths today, were from being stuck in a broken part of the map.  Jump on a rock to get a view of something, the rock isnt rendered properly, and im now stuck in an infinite hop up and down with no way to get out.  Can't jump because you aren't touching the ground.  Stuck there until someone comes to kill you.  Which is easy because you are constantly making the jumping and landing sounds. 

The quests are difficult in and of themselves because the loot you need is randomly spawned on the map.  So you have no idea where what you need is, and if you do happen to go to the right area, more than likely its already been picked clean.
Progressing with factions is at the speed of a snail, because it takes multiple drop-in's to find half the stuff you need for a quest, and multiple quests to gain a slight faction increase.

The sustainability is super shitty.  In tarkov, if you die and are low on money, you can load in as a scav and get at least a random loadout, some random items, and can potentially make some money.  In The Cycle, if you die, you lose your shit.  Then you do it again, and again, and now you are broke.  So what now?  Nothing, you are now broke and have nothing you can do.  The price of a "decent" gun is 25k, the cost of a full backpack on extract, assuming you sell EVERYTHING, is roughly 4k-10k.   If you buy a base tier gun, load in, and come across a player with anything better than the base armor, you cant pen their armor, so you cant do damage, so you are gonna die.  Rinse and repeat, you are now broke again.  There is no way to dig yourself out of the hole once you sink in it.  

The gunfighting is so sloppy and unreliable.  You can fight an npc monster, and while its strafing left or right, you aim dead on, hit, aim dead on, miss, lead the shot, miss, shoot behind it, hit.   Its all over the place.   Fighting a player is even worse.  Shoot a couple shots, and you get hit markers for shots you think you missed, and dont hit when you watch the shot go straight through them.  If you headshot someone, you either kill them, or do what seems like no damage.  

TLDR:
The game is very frustrating by itself, but add in people being dicks any way they can, you will just end up wasting hours of your time and regretting not doing literally anything else.
